stemBlocks: A plank of non-uniform density which has a mass of $15 \text{ kg}$ is used to make a see-saw. A pivot is placed under the centre of the plank as shown on the diagram. A boy of mass $35 \text{ kg}$ sits at one end of the plank with his centre of gravity $1.20 \text{ m}$ from the pivot. The see-saw balances when a woman of mass $60 \text{ kg}$ sits on the plank on the other side of the pivot. Her centre of gravity is $0.80 \text{ m}$ from the pivot. Where is the centre of gravity of the plank and what is the magnitude of the force between the pivot and the plank? (The gravitational field strength $g$ is $10 \text{ N kg}^{-1}.)$
